On this contract the stock stop wins under 1% of paths, so the bolded R:R above describes an outcome the simulation almost never reached, and its term contributes exactly nothing to the edge below. Largest-remainder allocation can round a genuinely non-zero share down to 0%, so “never” would be too strong; “contributes nothing” is exact, because the edge is weighted with that same allocated 0.

Every row sums to 100% because each of the [path count] simulated paths is counted once, for whichever barrier it reached first. The Monte Carlo card above measures each barrier on its own, so its numbers can sum past 100%.
The medians are conditional: “[days] to [target percentage]” is the median over the paths that got there first, not over all paths.
Priced at each barrier’s own median day, so time decay is included.

For the immediate figure — what this stop costs if it is hit right now — see “Max loss if the stop is hit” on the Arithmetic Profit Target card. The two differ by time decay AND by pricing model: that one is a delta-linear estimate at today’s price, capped at the premium, while these are repriced by the simulation. The two time bases must remain explicit.

mc.text: Only the first ratio is a measurement. Its risk leg is the premium minus what the contract would still be worth at the stock stop, which depends on strike, spot, time and IV independently — so it genuinely differs between contracts. The greyed one divides two numbers that are both a fixed fraction of premium, so premium cancels out of it entirely and nothing about this contract survives into the result. It is the same on every contract you could pick, which is why it is greyed. Deliberately not written as a division of the two percentages shown above: both are rounded for display while the stop fraction is an arbitrary number, so working it out from them disagrees with the printed ratio on roughly two rows in five.
The “Neither” term is the mean value of those paths at expiry minus the premium paid. It is signed, not a loss — those paths can end above what you paid.
Assumes implied volatility is unchanged when a barrier is reached. On a long call that is pessimistic at the stop and optimistic at the target — a real fear bid would leave more premium than shown.

$[premium] premium - $[remaining value] at the stop (repriced at [days] — the median day any path reaches the stop) = $[risk]

Invalidation is the editable execution stock stop. The scan supplies a structural/ATR stop (or legacy fallback); an Arithmetic calculation does not automatically replace this field. It also remains functionally load-bearing, not just a display figure: Send to broker stays disabled (“Invalidation stop required”) whenever this field is missing, regardless of what the Arithmetic card’s stop shows — the two are not just independently-displayed numbers, one of them is a hard submit gate the other has no relationship to.
